title: Lightweight credential debouncer and async-iterator sugar for Go SDK
author: Luis Montoya
release_notes: Go SDK v1.9.0: add credential debouncer + ergonomic async-iterator helpers; smaller API surfaces to reduce auth churn; minor performance/regression fixes; no breaking changes.
description:
Motivation: customer integrations and internal services observed thrashing when multiple goroutines raced to refresh credentials during transient auth failures. This PR introduces a lightweight credential debouncer (CredDebouncer) and a small set of ergonomic async-iterator helpers (StreamIter sugar) in the Go SDK to reduce repeated refresh attempts, simplify streaming consumer code, and align behavior with recent TS/Python ergonomics.

Goals: reduce duplicate refresh calls under high concurrency, expose an easy-to-use iterator wrapper for streaming responses, provide retry hooks tied to debouncer telemetry, and bump the Go SDK minor version.

What this PR does (summary):
- Add cred/debouncer.go: CredDebouncer with pooled singleflight-like semantics, TTL-aware backoff, and optional jitter. Exposes Debounce(ctx, key, refreshFunc) -> error + telemetry hooks.
- Add stream/iter_helpers.go: StreamIter accepts existing channel-based streams and returns a simple Next(ctx) (item, eof, err) facade designed for idiomatic Go loops; includes Cancelable() and PauseHint() methods used by higher-level SDK callers.
- Add retry/presets.go: small retry presets used by CredDebouncer (fast-fail, conservative-retry) to harmonize with TS/Py profiles.
- Wire cred debouncer into client/session.go: SDK's internal session provisioning uses CredDebouncer to ensure only one concurrent refresh per session key; existing cache semantics preserved.
- Tests: unit tests for debouncer concurrency, iterator behavior, and end-to-end e2e fixture that simulates intermittent auth failures.
- Docs: examples in examples/streaming/README.md showing simplified streaming consumer patterns and notes on when to use the debouncer.

Behavioral notes:
- CredDebouncer uses an internal singleflight keyed by session token + scope; when a refreshFunc is running, subsequent callers await the result instead of issuing parallel refreshes. If the underlying refresh fails with a 401-like (per remote code), the debouncer applies an exponential backoff window for that key before allowing another attempt. Debouncer exposes a Hook interface used by telemetry to record dedup counts and backoff durations.
- StreamIter is intentionally minimal: most SDK users previously wiring for-range over a channel can now call: for { item, eof, err := iter.Next(ctx); if err != nil { ... }; if eof { break } ... }. This improves ergonomics around context cancellation and makes it easier to attach per-item backpressure hints.

Compatibility and parity:
- The retry presets were designed to mirror the conservative vs aggressive profiles in the TS/Py SDKs so that multi-language services maintain similar retry behavior. The public API surface is additive; no breaking changes were introduced.

Testing and CI:
- Initial CI run reported a race in debouncer_test under -race; fixed by adding a short jitter and explicit ordering in the test harness (see commit d4f0c39).
- CI checks: go vet (pass), golangci-lint (pass), unit tests (-race) (pass after fix), integration fixture (pass), benchmark smoke (skipped on CI). Full pipeline green on rerun.

Review conversation (high level):
- Anya Patel (reviewer): "Can we avoid exposing the Hook interface publicly? I think we should keep telemetry plumbing internal and provide a RegisterTelemetry(func(...)) instead."
- Author (Luis): "Agree, adjusted — Hook is now an internal type and we expose RegisterDebouncerReporter in internal/telemetry. Updated tests accordingly."
- Noah Li: "Session integration looks good; please add a small opt-out for callers that absolutely want to bypass debouncing (internal migration path)."
- Luis: "Added ClientOptions{DisableCredDebouncer: true} and a migration note in CHANGELOG.md."
- Rina Gomez: "Add a follow-up task to verify perf at scale with Dedicated capacity — we observed a 3-5% improvement in synthetic load tests but want a canary on Dedicated."
- Luis: "Filed ENG-2199 to coordinate a Dedicated canary run."

Risk, rollout, and observability:
- Rollout plan was staged: feature gated behind ClientOptions and enabled by default for new minor. We cut a Go SDK v1.9.0 branch and published release candidates to internal channels first.
- Observability: debouncer emits counters for deduped refreshes and backoff windows; added to the telemetry dashboard (internal) and a short KB in docs/observability.md.

Follow-ups (future work):
- Evaluate integrating a shared cross-language debouncer control plane for multi-process deployments (ENG-2145).
- Add a lightweight priority hint so critical requests can bypass backoff for immediate refresh (careful with rate limits).

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main. Release notes updated and a Go SDK release (v1.9.0) cut after internal candidate validation.

If you want to try the new iterator: see examples/streaming/README.md for a minimal snippet. If you want to opt-out of automatic debouncing for any reason set ClientOptions.DisableCredDebouncer = true when constructing the client.
